title: Robotics and Task Transfer
summary: Studying how learned behaviors can generalize — so a robotic system trained on one task can adapt to another with a fraction of the data.
problem: Every time a robotic system is trained on a new task, we start nearly from scratch. The skills learned in one context — grasping, navigating, manipulating — rarely transfer cleanly to the next. This is not a problem of insufficient compute. It is a problem of representation and generalization that we do not yet understand well enough to solve reliably.
approach: Neryva's robotics program focuses on the transfer problem: what properties of a learned skill make it reusable, and how do we build training regimes that produce transferable behaviors rather than task-specific solutions. Our interest is in reducing the data cost of each new task — not by scaling training, but by learning in a way that generalizes.

vectors.title: Skill Generalization
vectors.description: Investigating under what conditions a learned policy transfers to an unseen task without catastrophic forgetting of previously learned behaviors.

vectors.title: Data-Efficient Adaptation
vectors.description: Quantifying how much task-specific demonstration data is genuinely required for reliable adaptation, and identifying methods that systematically reduce that threshold.

vectors.title: Task and Environment Representation
vectors.description: Determining what representations of task structure and environment state support the broadest transfer across physically different but conceptually similar tasks.

currentWork: Surveying transfer learning and meta-learning approaches in robotic manipulation and locomotion. Identifying the experimental settings where transfer fails most predictably — as a starting point for understanding why.
futureDirection: Developing low-data adaptation methods for manipulation tasks in unstructured environments, with a specific focus on settings where demonstration data is expensive or unsafe to collect at scale.

foundations.title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks
foundations.relevance: The clearest formulation of fast task adaptation through meta-learning. A conceptual anchor for understanding what task-level generalization requires.

foundations.title: Learning to Transfer: A Hierarchical List-wise Approach for Source Domain Selection in Transfer Learning
foundations.relevance: Addresses a key practical question: given a library of learned skills, how do we identify which ones transfer to a new task?

foundations.title: RoboAgent: Generalization and Efficiency in Robot Manipulation via Semantic Augmentations and Action Chunking
foundations.relevance: Recent work on building generalizable manipulation policies with limited data. Useful for understanding the current practical frontier.
